newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle active at $68.00 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle active at $68.00 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold at $68.00 per cwt, steady with last week, in active trading after midday on Wednesday, feedlot sources said.

About 33,900 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, USDA said. There were 57,400 head confirmed in the Panhandle for the week to date, which includes 22,600 formulated cattle to be shipped this week.
In Kansas, 36,500 head traded, which brought the week to date to 45,000 confirmed, including 5,800 head or about 13 percent prevously contracted or formulated cattle.
Fed cattle prices had been expected to trade unchanged with last week's price amid ideas that packers were short-bought on live inventory.
The strong cattle demand offset potential weakness from steep declines in beef prices this week, cattle sources said.
Beef prices were quoted down $1.34 to $1.82 per cwt, with 398 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA said.
The heavyweight choice beef was down $1.82 at $102.84, reflecting a drop of $4.95 for the week, USDA statistics showed.
